prompt: The bar chart below shows the average number of hours of sunshine per day in two cities in each season of 2020. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.
model:
The bar chart compares the average hours of daily sunshine in Lisbon and Oslo across the four seasons of 2020.

Overall, Lisbon received far more sunshine than Oslo in every season. In both cities, summer was the sunniest season, and winter was the dullest.

In Lisbon, sunshine rose steadily from 5 hours a day in winter to 8 in spring and 11 in summer, before falling back to 6 in autumn. That autumn figure was still above the winter figure.

Oslo followed a similar shape at a much lower level. Its sunshine peaked at 7 hours in summer and fell to only 1 hour a day in winter, the lowest value on the chart. Its autumn figure of 2 hours was also low, so the city had relatively little sunshine outside the summer months. The gap between the two cities was narrowest in spring, when Lisbon had 8 hours a day and Oslo had 5. Both cities therefore followed the same seasonal pattern, although Lisbon's figures were consistently higher.
notes: Band 7: the overview gives the general pattern for both cities without figures, the body groups the data by city, and each figure is taken exactly from the chart. Band 6 lists each bar in turn with no overview and no comparison.
band6: In Lisbon the sun is more in summer, it was 11 hours and in winter it was 5. In Oslo the sun is less, the winter was 1 hour and the summer was 7 hours. Lisbon has more sunshine than Oslo in all the seasons. The autumn is also not so sunny in both places. So Lisbon is more sunny in all the time.

criteria.tr: Band 7 gives an overview of the general pattern and reports exact values for both cities; band 6 lists the bars without a clear overall picture.
criteria.cc: Band 7 moves from the overview to each city and then compares them; band 6 describes the bars one by one with few linking devices.
criteria.lr: Band 7 uses 'far more', 'dullest' and 'narrowest' accurately; band 6 repeats 'more' and 'the sun' without variation.
criteria.gra: Band 7 uses comparatives and past forms accurately ('rose steadily from', 'was narrowest in'); band 6 has tense and article slips.
